facts.raw_span: 20-year history of progressive ataxia
8-month history of 'spasms' in his throat
difficulty with gait progressed after cessation of alcohol use
Hypometric saccades
Truncal and limb ataxia
Decreased vibratory sense with inability to ambulate
Bradykinesia and mild rigidity
Palatal myoclonus at a frequency of 1-2 Hz
Patient was unable to stop myoclonus of the palate with voluntary use of the palatal musculature
No clicking was noted by patient or examiners
Results of testing for spinocerebellar ataxia types 1, 2, 3, 6, and 12 were normal
Severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy

concepts.why: The combination of progressive ataxia, hypometric saccades, truncal and limb ataxia, decreased vibratory sense, bradykinesia, mild rigidity, and palatal myoclonus, along with severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy, is consistent with Multiple System Atrophy.

The 20-year history of progressive ataxia and difficulty with gait, despite normal genetic testing for certain types of spinocerebellar ataxia, suggests a possible diagnosis of spinocerebellar ataxia, although the specific type is unclear.
The presence of severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy, along with palatal myoclonus and other symptoms, is consistent with Olivopontocerebellar Atrophy, a subtype of Multiple System Atrophy.
The combination of hypometric saccades, bradykinesia, mild rigidity, and palatal myoclonus, along with severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy, is also consistent with Progressive Supranuclear Palsy.
The presence of bradykinesia, mild rigidity, and palatal myoclonus, along with severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy, is also consistent with Corticobasal Degeneration.

rationales.F07: Bradykinesia and mild rigidity are characteristic of Parkinsonian disorders, including Multiple System Atrophy

rationales.F12: Severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy is consistent with Multiple System Atrophy and Olivopontocerebellar Atrophy
